title: Malmgren's IDA job as cover for NSC work

tellings.quote: My work at the IDA was actually a cover for what I was doing for the National Security Council and the president.

Institute for Defense Analysis was an FFRDC back in the day and Harold Malmgrren was there and he even said on record uh that was a not official cover for like what I was actually doing for the National Security Council.
tellings.difference: Adds that IDA was a federally funded research centre (FFRDC) and calls it an 'unofficial' cover. Bissell is not mentioned.
tellings.link_reason: Same claim from Malmgren that his job at the Institute for Defense Analyses (IDA) was a cover for National Security Council (NSC) work, told by the host.

as_told.title: Malmgren's IDA job as cover for NSC work

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, repeats a claim by Harald Malmgren, a former advisor to US presidents, about his work in the 1960s and 70s. Malmgren says his job at the Institute for Defense Analyses, a research organisation funded by the federal government, was really an unofficial cover for what he was doing for the National Security Council, the White House body that advises the president on security. Michels tells it because it would mean Malmgren was closer to secret presidential matters than his job title suggested.
